title: UPDATE: Google's First Open Multimodal Embedding Model Powers Local Foresight App

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
A new voice-note recording application for macOS now uses local AI to construct knowledge graphs from Google Drive without cloud connectivity. The Foresight app, launched by Google, pairs its EmbeddingGemma 2 model with local versions of Gemma 4, specifically the E4B or 12B variants, to transcribe audio and organize data entirely on the user's device. The model's adoption by the developer community was immediate, with day-0 integration from AI framework providers including vLLM, Ollama, SGLang, and llama.cpp.

The 740M parameter model allows for the unification of text, code, images, video, and audio within a shared embedding space, utilizing between 191MB and 567MB of active RAM. In performance tests, the storage for 10M vectors was compressed from 30GB down to 0.4GB of RAM using 1-bit TurboQuant and Matryoshka Representation Learning. This 77x memory reduction was achieved while retaining 94.5% of the baseline retrieval quality.

Introducing EmbeddingGemma 2, a new open multimodal model that sets the standard for on-device efficiency.

- our first open, natively multimodal embedding model
- handles text, code, image, video, and audio tasks within a lightweight, modular 740M parameter form factor
- ideal for offline, privacy-first RAG when paired with Gemma 4
- outperforms some specialist models more than twice its size

Weights available now on Hugging Face.

SGLang has Day-0 support for EmbeddingGemma 2 from @GoogleDeepMind!

EmbeddingGemma 2 is a multimodal embedding model. It maps text, code, images, video, and audio into one shared 768d embedding space.
- 4 modalities with interleaved inputs, 8K context, 100+ languages
- Flexible footprint: modular encoders from 270M (text-only) to 740M (all modalities), plus Matryoshka embeddings

Get started with SGLang

selectedTweets.text:
Best-in-class for its size at 740M parameters, EmbeddingGemma 2 outperforms some models over twice its size while using from as little as ~191MB to 567MB of active RAM.

It also features a 4x larger 8K context window than the first generation, processing up to 5.5 minutes of audio, 29 images, or 58 video frames in one pass.

float32, 768 dims: ~30GB
1-bit TurboQuant: ~1GB (99% nDCG@10 kept)
+ MRL to 256 dims: ~0.4GB (94.5% kept with rescoring)

selectedTweets.bestBit: 128d gives 6x smaller vectors, but the quality tradeoff is notable
selectedTweets.text:
128d gives 6x smaller vectors, but the quality tradeoff is notable: MMEB v2 overall drops from 59.01 at 768d to 45.65 at 128d.

The card positions 128d for text-only workloads. For mixed modalities, the quality impact is much smaller at 256d. https://t.co/IiLyP4NBfp
